hook.text: An airline buys oil futures to lock in fuel prices. A trader buys puts to protect a stock position. Both are hedging.

buildup.text: Hedging is taking an offsetting position to reduce risk. It costs money but limits worst-case outcomes.

discovery.text: Common hedges: buying puts on stocks you own, shorting an index against long positions, or holding cash.

twist.text: Perfect hedges eliminate all risk—and all profit. Partial hedges reduce risk while preserving some upside.

climax.text: Hedging is insurance. Most of the time it costs you. The one time it pays off, it saves your portfolio.

punchline.text: Hedging costs are the price of sleeping at night.

quiz.question: What is hedging in trading?
options: Taking an offsetting position to reduce risk
Doubling down on a winning trade
